title: Jonah and the Letter
premise: In 1747, Gideon Montrose has lived twenty years as a man to inherit her dead master's mapmaking trade, and the atlas he died protecting contains more than coastlines: hidden in its marginalia are the names of townspeople who smuggled fugitives out of the country. When the army requisitions the harbor town and seizes the workshop's ledgers, a sympathetic clerk tips her off that the atlas itself will hang forty families if it reaches the colonial office. Over three desperate days, Gideon must copy, conceal, and carry the evidence past three military checkpoints to a departing ship, while an old army friend of her master's closes in who knew her father — and may know what she truly is. She reaches the ship at dawn, but only by surrendering the original atlas to the fire and trusting her memory and one copied page to survive; in the end she signs her own name for the first time in twenty years.
about_author: August Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing port records and requisition ledgers from the eighteenth century. They write historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: Gideon finishes the final plate of her dead master's atlas, inking the last coastline by candlelight. POV: Gideon. We learn she signs his name, never her own, and that certain names crowd the margins. Emotional beat: quiet pride shadowed by the fear of being found out — both as forger of identity and keeper of dangerous paper.

chapters.title: Red Coats at the Door
chapters.summary: Soldiers march into Harborwick at first light, nailing requisition notices to every post. The town's boats are seized, the countinghouse commandeered. POV: Gideon, watching from the workshop window. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve as she realizes the army doesn't just want the harbor — it wants records.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Knows
chapters.summary: A nervous army clerk, Elias Finch, arrives to inventory the workshop and lingers over the atlas margins with narrowed eyes. Gideon deflects him, but that night she checks the hidden names against her memory of the smuggling years. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: the past surfacing; she counts forty names and forty gallows.

chapters.title: The Master's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Gideon learning from Master Corvus why he marked the margins, and the night soldiers came for him. POV: Gideon in memory. Emotional beat: grief reframed — she understands now that he trained her not just in maps but in survival, and that finishing the atlas was always a trap she inherited willingly.

chapters.title: A Visitor Who Knew Her Father
chapters.summary: Captain Aldous Wren arrives to oversee the requisition — an old comrade of Corvus's army days who studies Gideon too long and asks about 'the daughter no one speaks of.' POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: terror wearing a polite face; the two threats, the atlas and her identity, begin to braid together.

chapters.title: Forty Names
chapters.summary: Gideon visits the widow Tamsin Hale, whose husband's name leads the margin list, and finds the town already whispering about arrests in the next parish. POV: alternating Gideon and Tamsin. Emotional beat: shared fear becoming conspiracy; Tamsin gives her the name of a ship captain sailing on the morning tide three days hence.

chapters.title: The Copying
chapters.summary: By lamplight Gideon begins copying the marginalia onto chart offcuts small enough to sew into her coat lining, destroying each scrap of waste. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: obsessive focus as sanctuary; but Finch returns unexpectedly and nearly catches the wet ink, forcing her to hide pages inside a half-finished map of the marshes.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Bridge
chapters.summary: Gideon tests the route with a harmless delivery, learning the bridge checkpoint's rhythms — and that Wren has ordered all outgoing parcels searched. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: the plan meeting reality; she realizes she cannot carry the evidence herself without being searched, and must find someone the soldiers ignore.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Carries Fish
chapters.summary: She recruits Tam, a mute fish-boy who moves freely through checkpoints, and teaches him the hiding place in the marsh map without telling him what it means. POV: Tam, then Gideon. Emotional beat: reluctant trust; Gideon hates making a child complicit, echoing how Corvus once made her complicit.

chapters.title: Finch's Doubt
chapters.summary: Elias Finch, inventorying late, finds a scrap of burned margin-paper in the workshop grate and says nothing — but pockets it. POV: Finch. Emotional beat: his crisis of conscience; we see the army's brutality up close through him, and his choice to wait rather than report becomes the story's loose thread of mercy.

chapters.title: Wren's Offer
chapters.summary: Wren summons Gideon, shows her Corvus's old army letters, and offers her passage and a new life if she surrenders the atlas and testifies that the names were her master's doing alone. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened by threat; he knows something about her, and the offer is a leash disguised as mercy.

chapters.title: The Night Search
chapters.summary: Soldiers ransack the workshop overnight on Wren's orders. Gideon watches from the marshes as they tear apart her life's work, finding the atlas but not the marsh-map pages. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: loss transmuted to clarity — the original is lost either way, so only the copies matter now, and there is no going back.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Arrest
chapters.summary: Tamsin Hale is taken at dawn, the first name on the list made flesh. The town goes silent in the way Gideon knows too well. POV: Gideon and briefly Tamsin in custody. Emotional beat: guilt and fury; the price of survival is being paid by someone else, and Gideon decides the ship sails tomorrow whether she's ready or not.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Marsh Road
chapters.summary: Gideon retrieves the hidden pages from the marsh map and moves them to Tam's fish cart, walking the flooded road at night past the second checkpoint disguised as a tide-surveyor. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: fear mastered through craft; her mapmaker's knowledge of tides and ground is literally what keeps her alive.

chapters.title: What Wren Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren interrogates Tamsin and pieces together the truth about Corvus's daughter — and realizes the apprentice before him is she. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: his corruption revealed; he doesn't want justice, he wants leverage, and a woman pretending to be a man is worth more to him than forty smugglers.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: Tam is stopped at the bridge checkpoint; the soldiers find nothing, but Wren, tipped by a neighbor, doubles the watch and orders the harbor closed until the atlas is accounted for. POV: Tam and Gideon. Emotional beat: despair closing like a trap; the ship leaves at dawn and the third checkpoint is now impassable.

chapters.title: Finch's Choice
chapters.summary: Finch confronts Gideon privately, returns the burned scrap, and tells her Wren plans to search every soul at the quay — then looks away, leaving his own travel pass on the table. POV: Finch and Gideon. Emotional beat: grace from an unexpected quarter; the man who could have doomed her chooses instead to spend himself.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Quay
chapters.summary: Gideon walks onto the quay in daylight, using Finch's pass and her surveyor's authority, the copied names sewn into her coat, while Wren's men search cart by cart behind her. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: white-knuckle tension; she passes within arm's reach of Wren, who looks at her once and lets her go — for reasons she won't understand until later.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Aboard the ship, Gideon learns Wren has ordered the atlas burned as evidence of his own failure to secure it — covering his tracks, freeing the names, saving himself. POV: Gideon watching the smoke from the rail. Emotional beat: bitter vindication; the corrupt destroy their own proof, and survival comes not from heroism but from everyone's small self-interests aligning.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: As the ship clears the harbor, Tamsin is released for lack of evidence, and Tam the fish-boy waves from the pier. Gideon learns Wren let her pass because exposing her would have exposed his own decades-old debts to Corvus. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: complicated relief; power corrupted even her rescue, and she owes her life to another man's rot.

chapters.title: A New Coastline
chapters.summary: Weeks later, in a new port, Gideon begins a fresh atlas — honest charts this time, no ghosts in the margins. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: cautious hope; she rebuilds her trade among strangers who know nothing, testing whether a person can outlive her own silences.

chapters.title: Her Own Name
chapters.summary: On the title page of the new atlas, Gideon dips her pen and writes 'Gideon Montrose' — keeping the name, but claiming it as hers, chosen rather than stolen. A letter arrives from Tamsin: the forty families are safe, and the copied page hangs framed in the widow's kitchen. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: resolution and identity reclaimed; survival cost everything except the one thing she finally owns — her name.
